steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Inspect the source, effective configuration, launch script,
metrics, rollouts, debug probes and frozen evidence. Connect any unusual
implementation to observed behavior rather than treating it as causal by
appearance alone.

Do not launch training, use the network, or modify the historical snapshot.
Write one concise diagnosis to `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md`. State the
verdict, concrete root cause and causal evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms; do not implement a fix.
Let me start by exploring the workspace to understand the structure of this RL training experiment.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	set -euo pipefail
3	
4	ROOT=${AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}
5	VERL_ROOT=${VERL_ROOT:-${ROOT}/verl}
6	BUNDLE=${BUNDLE:-${ROOT}/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8}
7	DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-${ROOT}/data/tiny-gsm8k}
8	RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-pissa_residual_reference}
9	LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-${ROOT}/results}/experiment_logs}
10	
11	RAY_JOB_TMP=${RAY_JOB_TMP:-/tmp/autorl-ray-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-local}}
12	
13	mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}" "${RAY_JOB_TMP}"
14	mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}/metrics" "${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" "${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations"
15	export PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT}:${PYTHONPATH:-}
16	export HF_HOME=${ROOT}/hf-cache
17	export RAY_TMPDIR=${RAY_JOB_TMP}
18	export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
19	export WANDB_MODE=offline
20	export WANDB_DIR=${LOG_DIR}
21	export WANDB_DISABLE_CODE=true
22	export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=${LOG_DIR}/metrics/all_steps.jsonl
23	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
24	export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
25	# Skipjack exports this ROCm variable even on NVIDIA nodes. Ray propagates it
26	# together with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which verl rejects as ambiguous.
27	unset ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
28	export VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/base_kl_debug
29	export VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
30	export VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
31	
32	printf '%s\n' 'packaged-defective-snapshot' > "${LOG_DIR}/source_commit.txt"
33	python -m pip freeze > "${LOG_DIR}/environment-freeze.txt"
34	nvidia-smi -q > "${LOG_DIR}/nvidia-smi.txt"
35	
36	cd "${VERL_ROOT}"
37	python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
38	  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=10 \
39	  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
40	  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
41	  data.train_files="${DATA_DIR}/train.parquet" \
42	  data.val_files="${DATA_DIR}/validation.parquet" \
43	  data.train_batch_size=4 \
44	  data.max_prompt_length=256 \
45	  data.max_response_length=32 \
46	  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
47	  data.truncation=error \
48	  data.seed=2026 \
49	  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base" \
50	  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter" \
51	  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=8 \
52	  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=8 \
53	  +actor_rollout_ref.model.use_dora=False \
54	  +actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_residual_base=True \
55	  actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear \
56	  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
57	  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
58	  +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
59	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-5 \
60	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \
61	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=4 \
62	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
63	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=False \
64	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
65	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.05 \
66	  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \

file.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT=${AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE:-/workspace}
VERL_ROOT=${VERL_ROOT:-${ROOT}/verl}
BUNDLE=${BUNDLE:-${ROOT}/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8}
DATA_DIR=${DATA_DIR:-${ROOT}/data/tiny-gsm8k}
RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-pissa_residual_reference}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-${ROOT}/results}/experiment_logs}

RAY_JOB_TMP=${RAY_JOB_TMP:-/tmp/autorl-ray-${SLURM_JOB_ID:-local}}

mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}" "${RAY_JOB_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${LOG_DIR}/metrics" "${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" "${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations"
export PYTHONPATH=${VERL_ROOT}:${PYTHONPATH:-}
export HF_HOME=${ROOT}/hf-cache
export RAY_TMPDIR=${RAY_JOB_TMP}
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export WANDB_MODE=offline
export WANDB_DIR=${LOG_DIR}
export WANDB_DISABLE_CODE=true
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH=${LOG_DIR}/metrics/all_steps.jsonl
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn
# Skipjack exports this ROCm variable even on NVIDIA nodes. Ray propagates it
# together with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which verl rejects as ambiguous.
unset ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
export VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/base_kl_debug
export VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug
export VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR=${LOG_DIR}/rollout_policy_debug

printf '%s\n' 'packaged-defective-snapshot' > "${LOG_DIR}/source_commit.txt"
python -m pip freeze > "${LOG_DIR}/environment-freeze.txt"
nvidia-smi -q > "${LOG_DIR}/nvidia-smi.txt"

cd "${VERL_ROOT}"
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=10 \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="${DATA_DIR}/train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="${DATA_DIR}/validation.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=4 \
  data.max_prompt_length=256 \
  data.max_response_length=32 \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=2026 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.use_dora=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_residual_base=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.target_modules=all-linear \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=False \
  +actor_rollout_ref.model.override_config.attn_implementation=eager \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=2e-5 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.05 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.fsdp_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.mode=async \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.35 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=512 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_seqs=16 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.calculate_log_probs=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=0.8 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.temperature=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False \
  reward_model.reward_manager=naive \
  trainer.logger='[console,wandb,file]' \
  trainer.project_name=AutoRLBench-Minimal-RL \
  trainer.experiment_name="${RUN_NAME}" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1 \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_epochs=4 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=4 \
  trainer.default_local_dir="${LOG_DIR}/checkpoints-disabled" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="${LOG_DIR}/validation_generations" \
  trainer.log_val_generations=4 \
  +trainer.log_base_model_kl=True \
  +trainer.log_final_policy_health=True \
  2>&1 | tee "${LOG_DIR}/train.log"

self._register_dispatch_collect_info(
                "actor", dp_rank=self.ulysses_device_mesh["dp"].get_local_rank(), is_collect=is_collect
            )
        else:
            self._register_dispatch_collect_info("actor", dp_rank=self.rank, is_collect=True)

        self.ulysses_sharding_manager = FSDPUlyssesShardingManager(self.ulysses_device_mesh)
        self._lora_rank = self.config.model.get("lora_rank", 0)
        self._is_lora = self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path") is not None or self._lora_rank > 0
        self._is_svd_init = self.config.model.get("lora_residual_base", False)
        self._init_lora_state: dict = {}  # {param_name: CPU tensor} saved before FSDP wrap
        self._svd_ref_adapter_name: str | None = None
        self._debug_step0_base_kl_logged = False

        self.role = role
        assert self.role in ["actor", "rollout", "ref", "actor_rollout", "actor_rollout_ref"]

        self._is_actor = self.role in ["actor", "actor_rollout", "actor_rollout_ref"]
        self._is_rollout = self.role in ["rollout", "actor_rollout", "actor_rollout_ref"]
        self._is_ref = self.role in ["ref", "actor_rollout_ref"]
        self.use_orig_params = self.config.actor.fsdp_config.get("use_orig_params", False)
        if self._is_lora or self.config.model.get("use_dora", False):
            # Keep PEFT trainable params as original tensors so FSDP does not flatten
            # them together with frozen base weights and silently skip updates.
            self.use_orig_params = True

        # TODO(haibin.lin):
        # As of now the type of config is DictConfig, if we assign config.profiler with ProfilerConfig,
        # it will actually convert the ProfilerConfig dataclass back to a DictConfig.
        # We can still use ProfilerConfig for testing purpose (tests/utils/test_nvtx_profile.py)
        # as they provides DictConfig-like interface
        # The benefit of creating the dataclass config is to perform validation during __post_init__
        if self._is_actor:
            omega_profiler_config = config.actor.get("profiler", {})
        elif self._is_rollout:
            # NOTE: In colocation mode, rollout config may not take effect (follow the actor config)
            # This is for extendability in AsyncRL cases
            omega_profiler_config = config.rollout.get("profiler", {})
        elif self._is_ref:
            omega_profiler_config = config.ref.get("profiler", {})
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid role {self.role}, should be one of "
                "['actor', 'rollout', 'ref', 'actor_rollout', 'actor_rollout_ref']"
            )
        # omega_profiler_config is DictConfig
        # profiler_config is a ProfilerConfig dataclass
        profiler_config = omega_conf_to_dataclass(omega_profiler_config, dataclass_type=ProfilerConfig)
        if omega_profiler_config.get("tool", None) in ["npu", "nsys", "torch", "torch_memory"]:
            tool_config = omega_conf_to_dataclass(
                omega_profiler_config.get("tool_config", {}).get(omega_profiler_config.get("tool"))
            )
        else:
            tool_config = None
        DistProfilerExtension.__init__(
            self, DistProfiler(rank=self.rank, config=profiler_config, tool_config=tool_config)
        )

        self._is_offload_param = False
        self._is_offload_optimizer = False
        if self._is_actor:
            self._is_offload_param = self.config.actor.fsdp_config.get("param_offload", False)
            self._is_offload_optimizer = self.config.actor.fsdp_config.get("optimizer_offload", False)
        elif self._is_ref:
            # TODO: it seems that manual offload is slowly than FSDP offload
            self._is_offload_param = self.config.ref.fsdp_config.get("param_offload", False)

        # normalize config
        if self._is_actor:
            self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size *= self.config.rollout.n
            self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size //= self.device_mesh.size() // self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
            assert self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size > 0, (
                f"ppo_mini_batch_size {self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size} should be larger than 0 after "
                f"normalization"
            )
            # micro bsz
            if self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size is not None:
                self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size //= (
                    self.device_mesh.size() // self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
                )
                self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu = self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size

            if self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu is not None:
                assert self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size % self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu == 0, (
                    f"normalized ppo_mini_batch_size {self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size} should be divisible by "
                    f"ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu {self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu}"
                )
                assert self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size // self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu > 0, (
                    f"normalized ppo_mini_batch_size {self.config.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size} should be larger than "
                    f"ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu {self.config.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu}"
                )

        # normalize rollout config
        if self._is_rollout and self.config.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size is not None:
            self.config.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size //= (
                self.device_mesh.size() // self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size
            )

loop = get_event_loop()
            loop.run_until_complete(self.trainer_mode())

    async def rollout_mode(self):
        """Context switch hybridengine to rollout mode."""
        aggressive_empty_cache(force_sync=True)

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_param:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)

        peft_config = None
        rollout_sync_mode = "full_weights"
        peft_model = getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
        if hasattr(peft_model, "peft_config"):  # LoRA / DoRA
            peft_config = peft_model.peft_config.get("default", None)
            if self._is_svd_init and not self.base_sync_done:
                logger.info(
                    "Rollout first sync for SVD-init adapters uses the original pretrained base model "
                    "instead of merged residual weights so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path."
                )
                params = self._collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params(peft_config)
                # SVD-init variants (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA residual-base bundles) still run vLLM
                # with LoRA wrappers enabled, so pretrained full weights must target base_layer.*
                # keys just like the normal first-sync LoRA path.
                params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in params.items()}
                peft_config = None
                rollout_sync_mode = "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights"
            elif getattr(peft_config, "use_dora", False) or str(getattr(peft_config, "peft_type", "")).endswith(
                "ADALORA"
            ):
                logger.info(
                    "Rollout sync uses merged full weights for DoRA/AdaLoRA because "
                    "vLLM adapter loading is unsupported or unsafe for this PEFT type."
                )
                params = collect_merged_peft_params(module=self.actor_module_fsdp)
                peft_config = None
                rollout_sync_mode = "merged_full_weights"
            else:
                params = collect_lora_params(
                    module=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                    layered_summon=self.config.rollout.get("layered_summon", False),
                    base_sync_done=self.base_sync_done,
                )
                rollout_sync_mode = "lora_delta" if self.base_sync_done else "initial_base_plus_lora_named_weights"
                if not self.base_sync_done:
                    params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in params.items()}
        else:
            params = self.actor_module_fsdp.state_dict()

        if self.rank == 0:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                sync_stage = "rollout_sync_initial" if not self.base_sync_done else "rollout_sync_latest"
                debug_path = _write_rollout_policy_debug(
                    sync_stage,
                    {
                        "experiment_name": str(getattr(self, "experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                        "rank": int(self.rank),
                        "base_sync_done_before": bool(self.base_sync_done),
                        "is_svd_init": bool(self._is_svd_init),
                        "is_lora": bool(self._is_lora),
                        "rollout_sync_mode": rollout_sync_mode,
                        "rollout_model_path": str(self.config.model.path),
                        "rollout_has_peft_config": peft_config is not None,
                        "peft_type": str(getattr(peft_config, "peft_type", "none")) if peft_config is not None else "none",
                        "active_adapter": (
                            peft_model.active_adapters[0] if getattr(peft_model, "active_adapters", None) else None
                        ),
                        "lora_adapter_path": str(self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path", "")),
                    },
                )
                print(f"[DEBUG rollout policy] wrote {debug_path}")

        params = convert_weight_keys(
            params, getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
        )

        # Special handling for LoRA with sleep_level=2:
        # When sleep_level=2, base model weights are destroyed during each sleep cycle.
        # separately collect and update LoRA weights and base model weights through their respective interfaces.
        # Here: params contains LoRA weights, base_model_params contains base model weights.
        if peft_config is not None and getattr(self.rollout, "sleep_level", None) == 2:
            base_model_params = collect_lora_params(
                module=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                layered_summon=self.layered_summon,
                base_sync_done=False,
            )
            base_model_params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in base_model_params.items()}
            base_model_params = convert_weight_keys(
                base_model_params, getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
            )

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_param:
            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)

        set_expandable_segments(False)

actor_module.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})

        if self._is_lora:
            print("Applying LoRA to actor module")
            actor_module.enable_input_require_grads()

            lora_adapter_path = self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path")
            if lora_adapter_path is not None:
                from copy import deepcopy

                from peft import PeftConfig, PeftModel, set_peft_model_state_dict
                from peft.utils.save_and_load import load_peft_weights

                print(f"Loading pre-trained LoRA adapter to {role} from: {lora_adapter_path}")

                # Copy adapter to local if needed
                local_adapter_path = copy_to_local(lora_adapter_path, use_shm=self.config.model.get("use_shm", False))

                adapter_config = PeftConfig.from_pretrained(local_adapter_path)
                if self._is_svd_init:
                    # The checkpoint at model.path is already W_res. Re-running
                    # PiSSA/OLoRA initialization here would subtract another SVD
                    # delta before the saved adapter tensors are loaded.
                    adapter_config.init_lora_weights = False

                actor_module = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
                    actor_module,
                    local_adapter_path,
                    is_trainable=True,
                    config=adapter_config,
                    # PiSSA/SVD-init needs real adapter tensors during its
                    # initialization; meta tensors cannot accept the computed
                    # CUDA factors via set_data().
                    low_cpu_mem_usage=not self._is_svd_init,
                )
                peft_config = actor_module.peft_config["default"]
                # Ensure task_type is TaskType enum, not string
                if isinstance(peft_config.task_type, str):
                    peft_config.task_type = TaskType.CAUSAL_LM

                if self._is_svd_init:
                    deferred = 0
                    for name, param in actor_module.named_parameters():
                        if "lora_A" not in name and "lora_B" not in name:
                            continue
                        if getattr(param, "is_meta", False):
                            deferred += 1
                            continue
                        self._init_lora_state[name] = param.data.clone().cpu()

                    self._svd_ref_adapter_name = "_base_ref"
                    ref_config = deepcopy(peft_config)
                    ref_config.inference_mode = True
                    ref_config.init_lora_weights = False
                    actor_module.add_adapter(
                        self._svd_ref_adapter_name,
                        ref_config,
                        low_cpu_mem_usage=False,
                    )
                    ref_state = load_peft_weights(local_adapter_path, device="cpu")
                    set_peft_model_state_dict(
                        actor_module,
                        ref_state,
                        adapter_name=self._svd_ref_adapter_name,
                    )
                    for name, param in actor_module.named_parameters():
                        if f".{self._svd_ref_adapter_name}." in name:
                            param.requires_grad = False

                    if self.rank == 0:
                        if deferred > 0:
                            print(
                                f"[SVD-init ref] Deferred saving {deferred} initial adapter parameters "
                                "until after FSDP materialization."
                            )
                        else:
                            print(
                                f"[SVD-init ref] Saved {len(self._init_lora_state)} "
                                f"initial adapter parameters for correct ref computation."
                            )
                        print(
                            f"[SVD-init ref] Loaded frozen reference adapter '{self._svd_ref_adapter_name}' "
                            "for correct base-model KL computation."
                        )
                disabled_dropout = self._disable_lora_dropout(actor_module)
                if self.rank == 0 and disabled_dropout > 0:
                    print(f"[LoRA] Disabled {disabled_dropout} LoRA dropout modules on loaded adapter")
                self._maybe_freeze_lora_A(actor_module)

            else:
                # Convert config to regular Python types before creating PEFT model
                lora_config = {
                    "task_type": TaskType.CAUSAL_LM,
                    "r": self.config.model.lora_rank,
                    "lora_alpha": self.config.model.lora_alpha,
                    "use_dora": self.config.model.use_dora,
                    "target_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.target_modules),
                    "exclude_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.exclude_modules),
                    "bias": "none",
                }

                        policy_loss = policy_loss + kl_loss * self.config.kl_loss_coef
                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/kl_loss"] = kl_loss.detach().item() * loss_scale_factor

                    if "base_ref_log_prob" in model_inputs:
                        base_ref_log_prob = model_inputs["base_ref_log_prob"]
                        # Compare rollout/eval-mode policy log probs against the frozen reference.
                        # This keeps base-model KL on the same inference-style footing as standard LoRA evals.
                        negative_approx_base_kl = torch.clamp(
                            rollout_old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob, min=-20.0, max=20.0
                        )
                        base_model_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_base_kl, response_mask)
                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/base_model_kl"] = base_model_kl.detach().item()
                        global_step = int(data.meta_info.get("global_steps", -1))
                        if not self._debug_base_kl_once and torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0:
                            self._debug_base_kl_once = True
                            rollout_vs_current = rollout_old_log_prob - log_prob.detach()
                            current_vs_base = log_prob.detach() - base_ref_log_prob
                            debug_payload = {
                                "stage": "actor_update",
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "global_step": global_step,

                                "current_vs_base_diff_abs_mean": float(current_vs_base.abs().mean().item()),
                            }
                            debug_path = _write_base_kl_debug("actor_update", debug_payload)
                            print(f"[DEBUG actor-update base KL] wrote {debug_path}")

                    if self.config.use_dynamic_bsz:
                        # relative to the dynamic bsz
                        loss = policy_loss * loss_scale_factor
                    else:
                        loss = policy_loss * loss_scale_factor
                    if self.scaler is not None:
                        self.scaler.scale(loss).backward()
                    else:
                        loss.backward()

                    micro_batch_metrics["actor/pg_loss"] = pg_loss.detach().item() * loss_scale_factor
                    append_to_dict(metrics, micro_batch_metrics)

                self._maybe_dump_full_grads()
                grad_norm = self._optimizer_step()
                mini_batch_metrics = {"actor/grad_norm": grad_norm.detach().item()}
                append_to_dict(metrics, mini_batch_metrics)
        self.actor_optimizer.zero_grad()
        return metrics

if isinstance(normalized, dict):
                        data.meta_info = normalized

            if not isinstance(data.meta_info, dict):
                with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                    data.meta_info = dict(data.meta_info)
            if not isinstance(data.meta_info, dict):
                data.meta_info = {}

            pre_update_base_model_kl = None
            safe_base_ref_log_prob = None
            if data.meta_info.get("log_base_model_kl", False) and "base_ref_log_prob" not in data.batch:
                data = data.union(self._compute_base_log_prob_from_actor(data, output_key="base_ref_log_prob"))
                if "old_log_probs" in data.batch:
                    response_mask = data.batch.get("response_mask")
                    base_ref_log_prob = data.batch.get("base_ref_log_prob")
                    old_log_prob = data.batch.get("old_log_probs")
                    if response_mask is not None and base_ref_log_prob is not None and old_log_prob is not None:
                        negative_approx_base_kl = torch.clamp(old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
                        step0_base_model_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_base_kl, response_mask)
                        pre_update_base_model_kl = float(step0_base_model_kl.detach().item())
                        data.meta_info["debug_step0_base_model_kl"] = pre_update_base_model_kl
                        safe_base_ref_log_prob = base_ref_log_prob.detach().clone().cpu().contiguous()
                        global_step = int(data.meta_info.get("global_steps", -1))
                        if not self._debug_step0_base_kl_logged and self.rank == 0:
                            self._debug_step0_base_kl_logged = True
                            debug_payload = {
                                "stage": "pre_update",
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "global_step": global_step,
                                "rank": int(self.rank),
                                **_debug_base_kl_payload(old_log_prob, base_ref_log_prob, response_mask),
                            }
                            debug_path = _write_base_kl_debug("pre_update", debug_payload)
                            print(f"[DEBUG pre-update base KL] wrote {debug_path}")
                # Base-model KL logging may offload the actor back to CPU; reload before training forward.
                if self._is_offload_param:
                    load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)

            if safe_base_ref_log_prob is None and "base_ref_log_prob" in data.batch:
                safe_base_ref_log_prob = data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"].detach().clone().cpu().contiguous()

            data = data.to("cpu")  # data will to device with each micro batch on actor.update_policy
            if safe_base_ref_log_prob is not None:
                # TensorDict may be locked after the device move; overwrite the existing slot in-place.
                data.batch.set_("base_ref_log_prob", safe_base_ref_log_prob)

            # perform training
            with Timer(name="update_policy", logger=None) as timer:
                metrics = self.actor.update_policy(data=data)
            if pre_update_base_model_kl is not None:
                metrics["actor/base_model_kl_pre_update"] = pre_update_base_model_kl
            delta_time = timer.last
            global_num_tokens = data.meta_info["global_token_num"]
            estimated_flops, promised_flops = self.flops_counter.estimate_flops(global_num_tokens, delta_time)
            metrics["perf/mfu/actor"] = (
                estimated_flops * self.config.actor.ppo_epochs / promised_flops / self.world_size
            )
            metrics["perf/max_memory_allocated_gb"] = get_torch_device().max_memory_allocated() / (1024**3)
            metrics["perf/max_memory_reserved_gb"] = get_torch_device().max_memory_reserved() / (1024**3)
            metrics["perf/cpu_memory_used_gb"] = psutil.virtual_memory().used / (1024**3)

            lr = self.actor_lr_scheduler.get_last_lr()[0]
            metrics["actor/lr"] = lr.item() if torch.is_tensor(lr) else lr
            self.actor_lr_scheduler.step()

            # TODO: here, we should return all metrics
            output = DataProto(meta_info={"metrics": metrics})

            output = output.to("cpu")

        if self._is_offload_param:
            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload actor model during update_actor", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_optimizer:
            offload_fsdp_optimizer(optimizer=self.actor_optimizer)
            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload actor optimizer during update_actor", logger=logger)

        return output

if self.async_rollout_mode:
            gen_batch.non_tensor_batch.update(batch.non_tensor_batch)

        return gen_batch

    def _validate(self):
        data_source_lst = []
        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
        log_final_policy_health = self.config.trainer.get("log_final_policy_health", False) and (
            self.global_steps >= self.total_training_steps
        )
        health_token_count = 0.0
        actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum = 0.0
        base_reference_abs_diff_sum = 0.0

        # Lists to collect samples for the table
        sample_inputs = []
        sample_outputs = []
        sample_gts = []
        sample_scores = []
        sample_turns = []
        sample_uids = []

        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)

            if "uid" not in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
                    [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(test_batch.batch))], dtype=object
                )

            # repeat test batch
            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
            )

            # we only do validation on rule-based rm
            if self.config.reward_model.enable and test_batch[0].non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["style"] == "model":
                return {}

            # Store original inputs
            input_ids = test_batch.batch["input_ids"]
            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)
            sample_uids.extend(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"])

            ground_truths = [
                item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in test_batch
            ]
            sample_gts.extend(ground_truths)

            test_gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(test_batch)
            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {
                "eos_token_id": self.tokenizer.eos_token_id,
                "pad_token_id": self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                "recompute_log_prob": False,
                "do_sample": self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample,
                "validate": True,
                "global_steps": self.global_steps,
            }
            print(f"test_gen_batch meta info: {test_gen_batch.meta_info}")

            # pad to be divisible by dp_size
            size_divisor = (
                self.actor_rollout_wg.world_size
                if not self.async_rollout_mode
                else self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers
            )
            test_gen_batch_padded, pad_size = pad_dataproto_to_divisor(test_gen_batch, size_divisor)
            if not self.async_rollout_mode:
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.actor_rollout_wg.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)
            else:
                test_output_gen_batch_padded = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(test_gen_batch_padded)

            # unpad
            test_output_gen_batch = unpad_dataproto(test_output_gen_batch_padded, pad_size=pad_size)

            print("validation generation end")

            # Store generated outputs
            output_ids = test_output_gen_batch.batch["responses"]
            output_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in output_ids]
            sample_outputs.extend(output_texts)

            test_batch = test_batch.union(test_output_gen_batch)
            test_batch.meta_info["validate"] = True

            if log_final_policy_health:
                response_mask = test_batch.batch["response_mask"].float()
                health_token_count += float(response_mask.sum().item())

                actor_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob(test_batch)
                if "rollout_log_probs" not in test_batch.batch:
                    raise RuntimeError("final policy-health validation requires rollout_log_probs")
                actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum += float(
                    (
                        (actor_log_prob.batch["old_log_probs"] - test_batch.batch["rollout_log_probs"]).abs()
                        * response_mask
                    )

def compute_log_prob(self, data: DataProto):
        # when is_lora is True, we use the actor without lora applied to calculate the log_prob
        # which is mostly used for ref log_prob calculation
        assert self._is_actor
        if self._is_offload_param:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)

        # Support all hardwares
        from contextlib import nullcontext

        is_lora = data.meta_info.pop("is_lora", False)
        adapter_ctx = self.actor.actor_module.disable_adapter() if is_lora else nullcontext()
        peft_model = getattr(self.actor, "actor_module", None)
        if self.rank == 0:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                debug_path = _write_rollout_policy_debug(
                    "actor_compute_log_prob",
                    {
                        "experiment_name": str(getattr(self, "experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                        "rank": int(self.rank),
                        **_actor_adapter_state_payload(peft_model, {"is_lora_flag": bool(is_lora)}),
                    },
                )
                print(f"[DEBUG actor compute_log_prob policy] wrote {debug_path}")
        # we should always recompute old_log_probs when it is HybridEngine
        data.meta_info["micro_batch_size"] = self.config.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu
        data.meta_info["max_token_len"] = self.config.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu
        data.meta_info["use_dynamic_bsz"] = self.config.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz
        data.meta_info["temperature"] = self.config.rollout.temperature
        # perform recompute log_prob
        with self.ulysses_sharding_manager:
            with adapter_ctx:
                output, entropys = self.actor.compute_log_prob(data=data, calculate_entropy=True)
            output = DataProto.from_dict(
                tensors={"old_log_probs": output, "entropys": entropys},
                meta_info={"temperature": self.config.rollout.temperature},
            )

        output = output.to("cpu")

        # https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/fsdp.html#fsdp-notes
        # unshard the root FSDP module
        if self.world_size > 1 and fsdp_version(self.actor.actor_module) == 1:
            self.actor.actor_module._handle.reshard(True)

        if self._is_offload_param:
            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload actor model during compute_log_prob", logger=logger)

        return output

Let me now put together all the evidence I've collected to understand the root cause of the issue. Let me look at a few more critical pieces.

Key observations so far:

1. **`actor/base_model_kl` is negative** across all steps (~-4to -5). KL divergence is always≥ 0, so this is clearly wrong. The metric is computed as `masked_mean(-negative_approx_base_kl, response_mask)` where `negative_approx_base_kl = rollout_old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob`. So `base_model_kl = masked_mean(-(rollout_old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob)) = masked_mean(base_ref_log_prob - rollout_old_log_prob)`. If this is negative, it means `rollout_old_log_prob > base_ref_log_prob` on average, i.e., the "base" reference log probs are LOWER (more negative) than the rollout log probs.

2. **`val-health/base_reference_consistency`: 0.046** — This metric is `exp(-base_reference_mae)` where `base_reference_mae` is the mean absolute difference between `compute_base_ref_log_prob` and `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob`. A value of 0.046 means `base_reference_mae ≈ 3.08` nats per token, which is enormous. This directly measures how far apart the actual "base reference" used during training is from the expected/correct one.

3. The debug shows `base_reference_mae = 3.083944` in the step4 metrics.

Now let me understand what's happening:

**The critical code path is `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor`:**

```python
def _compute_base_log_prob_from_actor(self, data: DataProto, output_key: str) -> DataProto:
    if self._is_lora:
        if self._is_svd_init:
            data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
            data = self.compute_log_prob(data)return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})

        # Standard LoRA/plus/b0: disable_adapter() exposes the underlying base model.
        data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
        data = self.compute_log_prob(data)
        return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})
```

For SVD-init (PiSSA), when `is_lora=True` is set and `compute_log_prob` is called:

```python
def compute_log_prob(self, data: DataProto):
    is_lora = data.meta_info.pop("is_lora", False)
    adapter_ctx = self.actor.actor_module.disable_adapter() if is_lora else nullcontext()
    ...
    with adapter_ctx:
        output, entropys = self.actor.compute_log_prob(data=data, calculate_entropy=True)
```

When `is_lora=True`, it calls `disable_adapter()`. For **standard LoRA**, `disable_adapter()` exposes the underlying base weights (the pretrained model), which is the correct reference. But for **PiSSA**, the base weights are `W_residual = W_pretrained - A_0* B_0` (the residual base after subtracting the initial adapter's contribution). So `disable_adapter()` on PiSSA's residual base returns the **residual weights**, NOT the original pretrained model weights. This makes the "base reference" completely wrong.

The correct approach for SVD-init should be to use `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` instead, which switches to the frozen initial adapter (`_base_ref`), so that `residual_base + A_0 * B_0 = W_pretrained`.

Wait, let me re-read...

Looking at `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor`:

For the SVD-init case:
```python
if self._is_svd_init:
    data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
    data = self.compute_log_prob(data)
    return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})
```

This sets `is_lora=True` which then calls `disable_adapter()`. But for PiSSA:
- The base weights = `W_residual` (not pretrained weights)
- The adapter = `A_0 * B_0` (initial PiSSA adapter)
- Full weights = `W_residual + A_0 * B_0 = W_pretrained`

So `disable_adapter()` exposes `W_residual`, which is **not** the original pretrained model. The function returns log probs computed with the **residual base** (missing the initial adapter contribution).

The correct computation for SVD-init would be to use the frozen initial adapter (`_base_ref`), which is exactly what `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` does via `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`. That switches to the frozen reference adapter (which has the initial PiSSA weights `A_0, B_0`) so that `W_residual + A_0 * B_0 = W_pretrained`.

So the root cause is: **`_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` uses `disable_adapter()` for SVD-init/PiSSA, which gives log probs under the residual base model (W_residual = W_pretrained - A_0*B_0) instead of the original pretrained model. This makes the base/reference log probs incorrect, causing negative KL values and a nearly zero `base_reference_consistency` (0.046).**

Wait, but what about `compute_ref_log_prob`? That calls `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor`, which means the **KL loss** is also wrong since it's computed using incorrect reference log probs! Let me check...

Looking at the KL loss computation in dp_actor.py:
```python
if self.config.use_kl_loss:
    ref_log_prob = model_inputs["ref_log_prob"]
    ...
    kld = kl_penalty(logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=self.config.kl_loss_type)
```

And `ref_log_prob` comes from `compute_ref_log_prob` which also calls `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` → `disable_adapter()`. So the KL loss uses residual-base log probs, not pretrained-base log probs.

The actor/base_model_kl is:
```python
negative_approx_base_kl = torch.clamp(rollout_old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
base_model_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_base_kl, response_mask)
```

So `base_model_kl = mean(base_ref_log_prob - rollout_old_log_prob)`.

The debug probe says:
- `base_ref_mean = -17.30` (log probs from the "base" reference = disable_adapter = residual base)
- `old_mean = -19.39` (rollout log probs from the current actor = residual_base + adapter)

So `base_ref > old`, meaning the residual base (without adapter) assigns higher log probs than the actor (residual_base + adapter). This is consistent with PiSSA where the adapter has been updated from initialization, making the actor diverge from the residual base.

But the actual pretrained model should give log probs somewhere in between. The `base_reference_consistency = 0.046` confirms a ~3 nat/token gap between `base_ref` (residual base without adapter) and `expected_base_ref` (residual base + initial adapter = pretrained).

And crucially: **all four uses of `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` are wrong for SVD-init/PiSSA**:
1. `compute_ref_log_prob` - uses residual base instead of pretrained as theRL reference
2. `compute_base_ref_log_prob` - same issue (wrong base reference)
3. The `log_base_model_kl` path in `fsdp_workers.py` line 1252

The only correct function is `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` which uses `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`.

Actually wait, let me re-examine `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` more carefully:

```python
def _compute_base_log_prob_from_actor(self, data: DataProto, output_key: str) -> DataProto:
    if self._is_lora:
        if self._is_svd_init:
            data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
            data = self.compute_log_prob(data)
            return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})

        # Standard LoRA/plus/b0: disable_adapter() exposes the underlying base model.
        data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
        data = self.compute_log_prob(data)
        return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})
```

Both branches do the exact same thing (`is_lora=True` → `disable_adapter()`). The SVD-init branch is supposed to do something different (use `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`), but it doesn't. It just falls through to the same logic as standard LoRA. This is the bug: the SVD-init branch was added as a code structure placeholder but doesn't actually implement the different behavior needed for PiSSA.

Wait, but what IS `disable_adapter()` doing for the SVD-init case? The base model loaded is `residual_base` (which is `W_pretrained - A_0*B_0`). When you disable the adapter, you get log probs under `W_residual = W_pretrained - A_0*B_0`. When the adapter is enabled, you get log probs under `W_residual + A_current*B_current`.

For the initial adapter, `A_current = A_0, B_current = B_0`, so the initial actor = pretrained model = `W_residual + A_0*B_0 = W_pretrained`. After training, `A_current, B_current` diverge from `A_0, B_0`.

The reference model should always be the pretrained model, i.e., `W_residual + A_0*B_0`. The frozen reference adapter (`_base_ref`) preserves `A_0, B_0`, which is exactly what `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` uses. But `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` uses `disable_adapter()` which gives `W_residual` without any adapter, which is WRONG.

So the root cause is: **`_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` calls `disable_adapter()` for the SVD-init case, which exposes only the residual base weights (`W_residual = W_pretrained - A_0*B_0`), not the pretrained model.** This wrong reference is used for:
- The KL loss (`ref_log_prob`)  
- The `base_model_kl` diagnostic metric
- The `base_reference_consistency` health check confirms this with a ~3 nat/token gap

The `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` correctly uses the frozen initial adapter to compute `W_residual + A_0*B_0 = W_pretrained`, and the 3.08 nats/token discrepancy between these two proves the wrong path is being used.

**Symptoms (downstream consequences):**
1. Negative `base_model_kl` (~-4 to -5): residual base assigns higher log probs than the updated actor → appears as if actor is diverging "backwards"
2. `base_reference_consistency` = 0.046 (should be ~1.0 if correct)
3. KL loss is computed against wrong reference (residual base vs pretrained), making it penalize the wrong distribution
4. Zero reward throughout training (possibly related, possibly because the model degrades: PPO with wrong reference = policy is being regularized toward a random reference)
5. pg_loss = 0.0 for steps1-3 (all advantages are zero because all rewards are zero)

Actually wait - `critic/advantages/mean: 0.0` and `critic/advantages/max: 0.0` across all steps until step 4... All rewards are 0 until step 4, so advantages are all zero. pg_loss is zero because advantages are zero. So the policy is only updated by the KL loss. But the KL loss is computed against the wrong reference.

Actually, actually... let me look more carefully. The `kl_loss` is non-zero (0.76, 0.93, 0.98, 0.88). This is the KL penalty between the actor and the "reference" model. # RL Training Run Diagnosis

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

---

## Root Cause

`_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` in `verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py` (lines 1531–1541) is broken for PiSSA / SVD-init adapters. Both the `_is_svd_init` branch and the standard-LoRA branch execute identically: they set `is_lora=True` and call `self.compute_log_prob(data)`, which routes through `disable_adapter()` at line 1415. For a standard LoRA model `disable_adapter()` correctly exposes the frozen pretrained weights. For a PiSSA model it does not — the base checkpoint loaded from disk is already `W_residual = W_pretrained − A₀B₀` (the residual after the initial SVD decomposition), so disabling the adapter exposes `W_residual`, not `W_pretrained`.

The correct reference for a PiSSA model is `W_residual + A₀B₀ = W_pretrained`, computed by activating the frozen initial adapter `_base_ref` via `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`. That path is implemented only in `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` (lines 1594–1611), which is used solely for the final health check, never for training.

Every call that goes through `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` therefore returns log-probabilities under `W_residual` instead of the pretrained model. This affects three live paths:

| Call site | Effect |
|---|---|
| `compute_ref_log_prob` (line 1558–1559) | KL-loss reference = `W_residual`, not `W_pretrained` |
| `compute_base_ref_log_prob` (line 1588–1590) | `base_model_kl` diagnostic uses wrong reference |
| Pre-update `log_base_model_kl` path (line 1251–1252) | Same wrong reference logged as `base_model_kl_pre_update` |

---

## Causal Evidence

**`val-health/base_reference_consistency = 0.0458`**  
This metric is `exp(−MAE)` where MAE is the mean absolute difference per response token between `compute_base_ref_log_prob` (the broken path) and `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` (the correct path). A value of 0.046 implies a mean absolute deviation of 3.08 nats/token — a gap that can only arise when two entirely different model distributions are being compared. The correct reference would give a value near 1.0; 0.046 is near-zero.

**`val-health/base_reference_mae = 3.084 nats/token`**  
Direct per-token average of `|base_ref_log_prob − expected_base_ref_log_prob|`. A 3-nat gap is large enough to move mass by a factor of ~e³ ≈ 20× across tokens, confirming the two paths compute under different model weights.

**`actor/base_model_kl` is negative across all four steps (−4.02, −4.61, −4.93, −4.61)**  
KL divergence is non-negative by definition. The metric is computed as `masked_mean(base_ref_log_prob − rollout_log_prob)` over response tokens. Negative values mean the "base reference" assigns lower log-probability than the actor on the generated response tokens. Under the correct pretrained reference a newly initialised PiSSA actor equals the pretrained model, and KL from actor to reference should start near zero then grow slowly. Negative values here confirm the reference is the degraded `W_residual`, not the pretrained model.

**Pre-update and actor-update debug probes (files `unknown_exp.pre_update.rank0.json`, `unknown_exp.actor_update.rank0.json`)**  
`masked_base_kl = −4.08` (pre-update step 1) and `masked_base_kl = −5.41` (inside the first actor update). All eight per-sequence `seq_base_kl_head` entries are negative. The probe at `actor_compute_log_prob.rank0.json` records `is_lora_flag: true, disable_adapter_layers: false` — the flag confirming the `disable_adapter()` branch was taken, with the adapter not yet disabled at the moment of capture.

**Source commit: `packaged-defective-snapshot`**  
The run's own `source_commit.txt` declares a defective snapshot.

---

## Symptoms (downstream; not root causes)

- **KL loss regularises toward the wrong distribution.** `actor/kl_loss` (0.76 → 0.93 → 0.98 → 0.88 nats) is non-zero because the actor diverges from `W_residual`, but `W_residual` is not the intended constraint. The policy is being pulled toward a model that is missing the principal-singular-value components of the pretrained weights.

- **Zero reward for 3 of 4 steps; zero advantages throughout steps 1–3.** `reward_components/acc_mean` is 0.0 for steps 1–3 (first nonzero only at step 4 with 0.125). Because all advantages are zero, `actor/pg_loss = 0.0` for those steps — no policy-gradient learning occurs. Only the misaligned KL loss updates the weights.

- **Diverging training perplexity.** `rollout_corr/training_ppl` rises from 2.74 (step 1) to 5.35 (step 2) before partially recovering, tracking the policy drifting away from its initialisation under a wrong KL anchor.

- **`val-health/actor_rollout_policy_agreement = 0.894`** (exp(−MAE) between actor log-probs and vLLM rollout log-probs). This is healthy on its own and confirms the actor–rollout synchronisation pipeline is functioning; the problem is not there.

---

## Distinction: Root Cause vs Symptoms

The single root cause is the missing `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` call in `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor`. All other observations — negative KL values, near-zero `base_reference_consistency`, wrong KL-loss target, stalled policy-gradient learning — are downstream consequences of using `W_residual` as the reference distribution wherever `W_pretrained` was required.

The run is **unhealthy**. Here is what I found and what I wrote to `/logs/artifacts/agent_answer.md`.

---

## Root Cause

`_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` in `verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py` lines 1531–1541 is broken for PiSSA / SVD-init adapters. The function has a dedicated `_is_svd_init` branch, but that branch is identical to the standard-LoRA branch: both set `is_lora=True` and call `self.compute_log_prob()`, which routes through `disable_adapter()`.

For **standard LoRA**, `disable_adapter()` correctly exposes the frozen pretrained base weights. For **PiSSA**, the base checkpoint on disk is already the residual `W_residual = W_pretrained − A₀B₀`, so disabling the adapter exposes `W_residual`, not the pretrained model.

The correct pretrained reference for PiSSA is `W_residual + A₀B₀`, which requires activating the frozen initial-adapter `_base_ref` via `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`. That path exists and is used correctly in `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` — but only for the final health check, never for training. Every training call goes through the broken path.

Three live paths are affected: `compute_ref_log_prob` (KL-loss reference), `compute_base_ref_log_prob` (`base_model_kl` metric), and the pre-update `log_base_model_kl` logging block.

---

## Causal Evidence

**`val-health/base_reference_consistency = 0.046`** — this is `exp(−MAE)` between the broken and correct reference paths per response token. A value of 0.046 means a 3.08-nat/token mean absolute gap. Two draws from the same distribution would give ≈ 1.0; 0.046 is near-zero and can only arise when the two paths run under different model weights.

**`val-health/base_reference_mae = 3.084 nats/token`** — quantifies that gap directly.

**`actor/base_model_kl` is negative every step (−4.0, −4.6, −4.9, −4.6)** — KL divergence is non-negative by definition. The metric is `masked_mean(base_ref_log_prob − rollout_log_prob)` over response tokens. Negative values mean the "reference" assigns lower probability than the actor on the generated tokens. Under the correct pretrained reference a freshly initialised PiSSA actor equals the pretrained model and KL should start near zero. Persistent negative values confirm the reference is the degraded `W_residual`.

**Debug probes confirm the code path taken.** `unknown_exp.actor_compute_log_prob.rank0.json` records `is_lora_flag: true`, confirming `disable_adapter()` was invoked. Both `pre_update` and `actor_update` debug files show `masked_base_kl` of −4.08 and −5.41, with all eight per-sequence entries in `seq_base_kl_head` negative.

---

## Symptoms (consequences, not causes)

- The KL loss (0.76–0.98 nats, coef 0.05) regularises the policy toward `W_residual` instead of the pretrained model, slowly degrading weights.
- Rewards are zero for 3 of 4 steps; advantages are zero throughout steps 1–3; `actor/pg_loss = 0` — no policy-gradient learning occurs, only the misaligned KL loss updates the model.
- Training perplexity diverges to 5.35 at step 2 before partially recovering, tracking policy drift under the wrong KL anchor.
- `actor_rollout_policy_agreement = 0.894` is healthy, confirming the actor–rollout sync pipeline is not the problem.
